title: Anand vs Carlsen, Game 9
summary: This game is remembered for the late promotion trick: Carlsen's pawn reached b1 with check and Anand's 28.Nf1 allowed a decisive pin. Watch how a double-edged position around the b-pawn and the blocked kingside decided everything in the last few moves.

moves.comment: 1.d4 opens the queen's pawn. The engine slightly preferred 1.e4, but 1.d4 is sound and the evaluation barely moves.
1...Nf6 develops the knight and eyes the centre. The engine rates it best, and the position stays level.
2.c4 builds a broad centre. The engine rates it best and the balance stays close to level.
2...e6 prepares ...d5 and keeps the position flexible. The engine rates it best.
3.Nc3 develops naturally. The engine preferred 3.g3, but the difference is small.
3...Bb4 pins nothing yet, but it invites a trade on c3 that would double White's pawns. The engine rates it best.
4.f3 supports a future e4 but weakens the diagonal to the king. The engine preferred 4.Qc2, so this is good rather than best.
4...d5 challenges the centre. The engine preferred 4...c5, though the move is still graded good.
5.a3 asks the bishop a direct question. The engine rates it best.
5...Bxc3+ gives up the bishop pair to double White's pawns. The engine preferred 5...Be7, and the evaluation stays even.
6.bxc3 recaptures and opens the b-file for White. The engine rates it best, with a slight edge to White.
6...c5 strikes at White's centre. The engine rates it best.
7.cxd5 opens the position. The engine rates it best and the evaluation is unchanged.
7...exd5 recaptures the pawn, though 7...Nxd5 was preferred. The evaluation drifts slightly toward White.
8.e3 solidifies the centre and opens the bishop on f1. The engine rates it best.
8...c4 gains queenside space and fixes the pawn. The engine preferred 8...Qc7, so this is good rather than best.
9.Ne2 reroutes the knight. The engine preferred 9.g4, which gains space at once, so this is good rather than best.
9...Nc6 develops the last minor piece. The engine rates it best.
10.g4 launches a kingside pawn advance. The engine rates it best and the evaluation holds.
10...O-O completes development. The engine preferred 10...Na5, though the difference is small.
11.Bg2 places the bishop on the long diagonal. The engine rates it best.
11...Na5 starts the knight's journey toward b3. The engine rates it best.
12.O-O castles. The engine preferred 12.Ra2, so this is good rather than best.
12...Nb3 plants the knight on an outpost beside White's rook. The engine rates it best.
13.Ra2 guards the second rank. The engine preferred 13.Rb1, so this is good rather than best.
13...b5 starts a queenside advance. The engine preferred 13...a5, though the change is small.
14.Ng3 brings the knight back into play. The engine preferred 14.e4, and the evaluation drifts toward Black.
14...a5 prepares to open the a-file. The engine rates it best.
15.g5 gains space but loosens the kingside. The engine preferred 15.e4, and the evaluation swings toward Black.
15...Ne8 retreats the knight. The engine preferred 15...Nxc1, so this is good rather than best.
16.e4 strikes at the centre and keeps the balance. The engine rates it best.
16...Nxc1 wins the bishop on c1, and White recaptures the knight next move. The engine rates it best.
17.Qxc1 recaptures the knight. The engine rates it best and the position stays level.
17...Ra6 puts the rook on the a-file. The engine preferred 17...Rb8, so this is good rather than best.
18.e5 gains space and attacks the knight on f6. The engine rates it best, and the evaluation dips toward Black.
18...Nc7 retreats to a passive square. The engine preferred 18...g6. This is an inaccuracy, and the balance swings to White.

moment.title: Passive knight retreat on c7
moment.text: After 18.e5 the knight on f6 is attacked, and 18...Nc7 steps back to a square where it does little. The engine preferred 18...g6, which keeps more defensive resources. The evaluation swings from roughly level to a clear edge for White, so this is the first real slip by Black.

moves.comment: 19.f4 supports the e5 pawn and prepares f5. The engine rates it best and White's edge grows.
19...b4 opens the queenside with a pawn lever. The engine rates it best, though the evaluation slips a little.
20.axb4 recaptures on b4. The engine preferred 20.f5, so this is good rather than best.
20...axb4 reopens the a-file for Black's rook. The engine rates it best.
21.Rxa6 exchanges rooks on the a-file. The engine rates it best.
21...Nxa6 recaptures with the knight. The engine rates it best and the evaluation stays close.
22.f5 gains kingside space. The engine preferred 22.h4, so this is good rather than best.
22...b3 pushes the pawn deep into White's camp. The engine preferred 22...g6, and the evaluation moves toward Black.

moment.title: Passed pawn pushed to b3
moment.text: 22...b3 creates a passed pawn that is deep in White's half of the board. The engine preferred 22...g6, and the evaluation moves toward Black after this push. Watch how this pawn ties down White's pieces on the queenside.

moves.comment: 23.Qf4 brings the queen to the kingside. The engine preferred 23.h4, and the evaluation is still slightly toward White.
23...Nc7 returns the knight to defence. The engine rates it best.
24.f6 attacks the g7 square but gives up control of e5. The engine preferred 24.h4. This is an inaccuracy and the balance tips to Black.

moment.title: 24.f6 loosens the e5 pawn
moment.text: White pushes f6 to attack the g7 square, but the pawn structure around e5 becomes weaker. The engine preferred 24.h4, and the evaluation falls from about plus six tenths to slightly favouring Black. This is an inaccuracy that handed Black counterplay.

moves.comment: 24...g6 challenges the pawn on f6. The engine preferred 24...gxf6, so this is good rather than best.
25.Qh4 brings the queen to the attack. The engine rates it best.
25...Ne8 retreats to guard the position. The engine rates it best.
26.Qh6 probes the kingside. The engine preferred 26.Ne2, which keeps the knight in play, so this is good rather than best.
26...b2 pushes the passed pawn to the second rank. The engine rates it best and the evaluation is level.
27.Rf4 tries to stop the pawn, but the engine preferred 27.Ne2. This is good rather than best.
27...b1=Q+ promotes with check along the first rank. The engine rates it best and the balance stays level.

moment.title: 27...b1=Q with check
moment.text: Black's pawn promotes on b1 with check along the first rank. This forces White to find a block, and the new queen becomes the focus of the position. The engine rates this move best, and the material count is still level.

moves.comment: 28.Nf1 blocks the check but allows a pin. The engine preferred 28.Bf1, and the evaluation collapses to about minus six.

moment.title: 28.Nf1 allows the decisive pin
moment.text: White's knight blocks the check, but the engine line Bf1 was far better. After 28.Nf1 the evaluation collapses from level to about minus six. The knight is then pinned against the king, and Black's queen dominates the first rank.

moves.comment: 28...Qe1 pins the knight on f1 against the king. The engine rates Black about six and a half pawns ahead, and Black won.

lessons: When a pawn is about to promote, check the back rank and every block square before you choose a defensive move.
A pawn push that attacks nothing directly can still weaken the squares behind it, so count the consequences before advancing.
Before a forcing sequence, compare the engine's preferred alternative, because a small inaccuracy can turn into a large swing later.
